supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:58 UTC, WS-ICHEN-01 (10.40.10.21:58691) sent 51,000,389 bytes (approximately 51 MB) to 10.40.20.30:8080 and received 9,017 bytes over a 9.03-second HTTP connection. This matches the alerted time and outbound volume.

The alerted connection terminates at the explicit proxy endpoint identified by the supplied inventory. Its connection record does not identify the ultimate destination, URL, initiating process, user, or transferred content; therefore it establishes a large workstation-to-proxy transfer, not malicious exfiltration or an approved upload.

Later AWS browsing is attributed to Chrome under ivy.chen on source ports 50262 and 52946. These are separate connections from the alerted source port 58691 and do not establish the destination or process responsible for the earlier transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor coverage report, which has no record ID, states that WS-ICHEN-01 winsec and Sysmon logs and PROXY-NWD-01 proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC. This includes the alerted connection in T039-00140.

Zeek connection telemetry preserves the alerted connection's endpoints, duration, and directional byte counts, but T039-00140 contains no ultimate destination, HTTP request details, payload, or endpoint process attribution. Healthy network sensor status does not supply those missing fields.
claims_not_established: Whether the bytes recorded in T039-00140 were forwarded externally, and to which ultimate destination.
Which process and user initiated T039-00140, what content was transferred, and whether the transfer was authorized.
Whether T039-00140 represents malicious exfiltration or benign business activity; volume and proxy use alone do not distinguish them.
Any connection between the alerted transfer and the later AWS browsing, ZSATunnel process, or LSASS access records.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy logs or upstream gateway records for 10.40.10.21:58691 to 10.40.20.30:8080 around 13:45:58 UTC, matching T039-00140, to identify the destination, request method, forwarding outcome, and authenticated user.
Recover local endpoint logs or EDR history for the alerted connection in T039-00140 to identify its initiating process, command line, parent process, user, and associated file accesses.
Obtain retained packet captures, destination-side upload or audit logs, or application history for T039-00140 to identify transferred content and verify business authorization.
unrelated_findings: T039-00264 and T039-00265 show ZSATunnel.exe starting as SYSTEM at 14:12:33 UTC. Review separately against the supplied no-VPN and approved-service inventory; these records do not establish a relationship to T039-00140.

T039-00306 records an ivy.chen CONNECT request to zoom.us denied with status 403 at 14:17:15 UTC. Review separately as an attempted use of a service absent from the supplied approved list; it does not explain the alerted transfer.

T039-00304 records svchost.exe accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess=0x1010 at 14:13:46 UTC. If investigated, treat it separately: this record alone establishes neither credential theft nor a connection to the earlier transfer.
